items.text:
Hi, I'm Andre. This is my take-home for Cerbo: an in-house supplement store, built as a vertical slice in Cerbo's own stack. Vue, TypeScript, Fastify, and Postgres.

The brief: a provider assembles a supplement order, the patient pays, and the system records exactly where every cent goes. Cost of goods, provider margin, and Cerbo's seventy-five basis point fee. Let me show you.

This is the order builder, styled to live inside Cerbo's chart. I'm acting as Doctor Welby. I pick Zeus King, and add Omega-3 and vitamin D.

Prices pre-fill from the practice default. I can override a line, or type a target margin and let the price derive. The billing panel shows the split live: order total, cost of goods, the platform fee, and the provider's margin after the fee.

When I send it, the order locks, and the patient gets what Cerbo would actually send: a secure portal message, and an email nudge.

Here's the patient side. Their portal shows the balance due, and the message with a pay button. Checkout is a plain card form. Only a token leaves the browser, never the card number.

Watch a declined card first. A four-oh-two comes back, and nothing is written. Now a good card. The receipt shows the card ending in four two four two.

If I refresh, it's still one payment. The idempotency key replays the original receipt.

This is the part that's graded. The ledger has exactly three entries for this order, each with a memo showing its computation.

The fee is seventy-five basis points of sixty-six dollars: forty-nine and a half cents, rounded half-up to fifty. Margin is the residual, so the sum is exact by construction.

And it's not just the app saying so. A deferred constraint trigger in Postgres re-checks the whole split at commit, the ledger rejects updates and deletes, and the tests prove it by trying to break it with raw SQL.
Reporting sums the ledger directly, so the tiles always reconcile with the per-order audits. Inventory moves when an order is paid, and it's flagged when it goes negative.

Under the hood: all money is integer cents. The split function is pure and property-tested. The integrity migration is the most important file in the repo.

Payments, identity, and messaging are stubbed behind documented seams, so a real processor, or Cerbo's own portal, plugs in without touching the routes.

It's deployed on Railway with CI on every push, sixty integration tests on a real Postgres, and an honest decision log, including where AI misled me.

Thanks for looking.
